title: Material X-Ray Post-Process Scanner
description: A ShaderBall sits on a pedestal while a CarbonFibre panel orbits around it as a scanning element. The user controls a radial wipe post-process effect that progressively reveals different post-processing layers — bloom, chromatic aberration, pixelation, and a custom edge-detection outline — simulating an industrial material scanner analyzing the ShaderBall's surface composition.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with EffectComposer from three/addons. Load ShaderBall.glb centered at origin and CarbonFibre.glb positioned as a flat vertical panel orbiting the ShaderBall at radius 3 on the XZ plane, rotating continuously like a scanner arm. Camera at (0, 2, 6) looking at origin with OrbitControls. Use a three-point lighting setup: warm key light upper-right, cool fill light left, rim light behind. Set background to dark charcoal gradient using a simple shader background. Build an EffectComposer pipeline with RenderPass, then UnrealBloomPass (strength 0.8, threshold 0.6), then ShaderPass for chromatic aberration, then ShaderPass for pixelation, and finally ShaderPass for Sobel edge-detection outline. Write a custom ShaderPass that acts as a radial wipe mixer: it takes a uniform float 'uReveal' (0 to 1) and a uniform vec2 'uCenter' representing screen-space center of the ShaderBall. Based on the distance from uCenter compared to uReveal, it blends between the clean render and the full post-processed result. Interaction steps: (1) User clicks a 'Begin Scan' button which starts the CarbonFibre panel orbiting and enables a slider. (2) User drags a horizontal slider labeled 'Scan Depth' from 0 to 100 which drives uReveal from 0.0 to 1.0, expanding the radial post-process wipe outward from the ShaderBall center. (3) User clicks one of four toggle buttons to switch which post-process effect is revealed: Bloom, Chromatic Aberration, Pixelation, or Edge Outline. (4) User can click the ShaderBall to reposition the radial wipe center to the click point in screen space. (5) A 'Capture' button freezes the current state and displays a small thumbnail preview in the corner. Style the UI overlay with semi-transparent dark panels and monospace font for a sci-fi scanner aesthetic. The CarbonFibre panel should have emissive edges that pulse in sync with the scan depth value.
